listenings.text: Quick update before Friday, everyone. Where do we stand on the payments mandate. First, the good news. We have already finished the impact model for all three scenarios, so we can put a number on the table whenever the client asks. Second, the open point. The client has not approved the restructuring of the holding yet, and until that decision arrives we cannot start the second phase. I have sent two reminders. Third, and this one is not negotiable. We must file the return under the old rules this week. The deadline does not move, and nobody in this room should assume that the reform changes it. So please deal with the filing first, and then we go back to the model.

People ask me what I actually pay a tax advisor for, and the answer surprises them. I do not pay for the rules. My team can read the law, and honestly the law is public. What I pay for is the sentence that comes after the rules. What I recommend is. Then one clear action, with a date. If an advisor sends me eleven pages describing what changed, I have learned nothing, because I already knew what changed. That is the moment I stop calling them and I look for someone else. The best advisor we have ever had used to open every call the same way. He would say, here is what you must do this quarter, and here is what I think you should do next year. Two sentences. That is the whole job.

extra_audio.text: We have already assessed the impact on the tax base. The client has not approved the restructuring yet. They must file a return under the current rules in September. After that, they should review the holding, so that we can mitigate risk.
